title: GitHub - gorse-io/clap.cpp: Audio embedding inference in pure C++ supports CLAP, MuQ, CLaMP3 and MERT with Python, Node and Rust bindings
excerpt: Audio embedding inference in pure C++ supports CLAP, MuQ, CLaMP3 and MERT with Python, Node and Rust bindings - gorse-io/clap.cpp
content_html:
C++20/ggml implementations of audio embedding inference features:

  • Supports WAV, MP3, and FLAC audio input.
  • Automatically resamples audio to the model's required.
  • Automatically mixes stereo and multichannel audio down to mono.

Supported models

Model Text Audio Embedding dimensions Sample rate
CLAP ✅ ✅ 512 48 kHz
CLAP2 Large ✅ ✅ 960 32 kHz
CLAP2 Medium ✅ ✅ 640 32 kHz
CLAP2 Small ✅ ✅ 512 32 kHz
CLAP2 XS ✅ ✅ 320 32 kHz
CLAP2 XXS ✅ ✅ 224 32 kHz
CLaMP3 ✅ ✅ 768 24 kHz
MERT v1 95M ❌ ✅ 768 24 kHz
MERT v1 330M ❌ ✅ 1,024 24 kHz
MERT v2 FullSong / 30s ❌ ✅ 1,024 24 kHz
MuQ ❌ ✅ 1,024 24 kHz
MuQ-MuLan ✅ ✅ 512 24 kHz

GGUF models are available at Audio Embedding GGUF collection.

Bindings

Binding CPU CUDA Vulkan Install
Python ✅ ✅ ✅ pip3 install clap-cpp
Rust ✅ ✅ ✅ cargo install clap-cpp
Node.js ✅ ❌ ❌ npm install clap-cpp

Usage

Embeddings command

Load a converted GGUF and generate real native text or audio embeddings:

clap embedding --model larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf --text 'Sound of a dog'
clap embedding --model larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf --audio dog.wav

Embeddings server

Start the server with a GGUF supporting the requested modality, such as CLAP, CLaMP3 or MuQ-MuLan (default listen address: 127.0.0.1:8080):

clap serve --model larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

The model is loaded once at startup. Its API identifier is the GGUF filename (larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf in this example), not its full path or a Hugging Face repository ID. Send an OpenAI-compatible text embeddings request:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf","input":["Sound of a dog"],"encoding_format":"float"}'

Audio inputs use one input_audio content block per item. Encode the complete WAV, MP3 or FLAC file as standard base64 (no whitespace or data-URL prefix):

audio_base64=$(base64 < dog.wav | tr -d '\r\n')
printf '{"input":[{"content":[{"type":"input_audio","input_audio":{"data":"%s"}}]}]}' "$audio_base64" |
  curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/embeddings \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @-

Audio search (brute force)

Search the esc5 audio directory recursively for dog and return the ten most related audio files:

clap search esc5 --model larger_clap_general-q4_k_m.gguf --text 'dog' --top-k 10
